intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have been perfecting their craft for generations and experience the authentic flavors of Tokyo's most iconic food destination.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Browse multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, explore retro game shops, visit maid cafes, and discover the latest in Japanese tech gadgets, robotics kits, and cutting-edge consumer electronics that define Japan's tech culture.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, at dawn before the crowds arrive. Stroll through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, explore the surrounding Asakusa district's old Edo-era atmosphere, and witness morning prayers and incense rituals for an authentic cultural experience.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture merge seamlessly. Walk through immersive, ever-changing rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art created by the renowned teamLab collective. A perfect fusion of Japan's tech innovation and artistic expression.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Izakaya Alley Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Venture into the narrow, lantern-lit alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and Kabukicho's hidden izakayas for an unforgettable evening of yakitori, ramen, sake, and Japanese whisky. Sit elbow-to-elbow with Tokyo locals, order seasonal small plates, and experience the convivial after-work dining culture that defines authentic Tokyo nightlife.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for convenient train travel throughout Tokyo. Take the airport limousine bus or Narita Express (N'EX) to central Tokyo and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your room and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport terminal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour convenience store (7-Eleven, Lawson, or FamilyMart) near the hotel – onigiri rice balls, hot noodles, and sandwiches available for under ¥600

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash (yen) at the airport for best rates. Japan is still largely cash-based. Pick up a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card at the airport arrival hall. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping later.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a slow start, explore the immediate neighborhood around the hotel. Visit a local shotengai (shopping street) or morning market to get a feel for daily Tokyo life. Stop by a nearby konbini (convenience store) to stock up on budget snacks and drinks for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Asakusa, one of Tokyo's most traditional districts. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), Tokyo's oldest and most famous Buddhist temple. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for affordable souvenirs, traditional snacks like ningyo-yaki and melonpan (¥100–¥300 each). Explore the surrounding Asakusa streets and admire the rickshaws and kimono-clad visitors.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sumida River and enjoy the view of Tokyo Skytree (lit up at night) from the riverside for free. Explore the Hoppy Street area in Asakusa for lively izakaya (Japanese pub) dining with locals.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast – onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea for under ¥400
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan or a local ramen shop near Senso-ji – budget ramen bowl for ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya – yakitori skewers, edamame, and a beer for approximately ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Asakusa is easily accessible by Tokyo Metro Ginza Line or Asakusa Line. April is cherry blossom season – check Sumida Park nearby for sakura viewing. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park (free entry), one of Tokyo's most beloved public parks and a top cherry blossom spot in April. Stroll through the park and visit the Ueno Tosho-gu Shrine (free). Browse the Tokyo National Museum exterior and grounds (museum entry ¥1,000 if interested in Japanese history and artifacts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akihabara – Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and tech/anime culture hub. Walk through multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Akiba, browse retro game shops, figure stores, and maid cafes. Visit Super Potato for vintage gaming nostalgia. Window shop for gadgets and tech accessories.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening exploration. Visit a multi-floor arcade (game center) like Taito Station or GiGO Akihabara – budget ¥500–¥1,000 for games. Experience the neon-lit streets at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if available, or a nearby bakery/konbini for ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Ueno area – try Ameyoko Market street food: takoyaki, yakisoba, or fresh seafood snacks for ¥300–¥600
meals.dinner: Akihabara – Curry House CoCo Ichibanya or a local ramen shop for ¥700–¥1,000. Alternatively, try a standing sushi bar for fresh and affordable sushi

day_by_day.notes: Ameyoko Market near Ueno is a bustling open-air market great for cheap street food and bargain shopping. Akihabara is a short train ride from Ueno on the JR Yamanote Line (¥140).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shibuya and witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing – the world's busiest pedestrian crossing. Visit Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for panoramic city views, or save money and view the crossing for free from the Starbucks window on the 2nd floor of Shibuya Tsutaya (just buy a coffee). Explore Shibuya 109 fashion building and surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Harajuku. Stroll down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion, crepes (¥400–¥700), and unique accessories. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) set in a peaceful forested area – a serene contrast to the busy streets outside.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Omotesando, Tokyo's upscale boulevard, for window shopping and people-watching (free). Head to nearby Shimokitazawa – a bohemian neighborhood with vintage clothing shops, live music bars, and cozy cafes perfect for a budget evening out.

meals.breakfast: Konbini or a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel for ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Harajuku – try a Harajuku crepe (¥400–¥700) and browse Takeshita Street snacks
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa – small local curry restaurant or izakaya with set meals for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is especially beautiful in April. Shimokitazawa has a thriving indie music scene – check local listings for free or cheap live shows (¥500–¥1,000 cover). Take the Odakyu Line from Shinjuku to Shimokitazawa (¥130).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku – start with a visit to the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:30 AM) for stunning 360-degree views of Tokyo, including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) – one of the best cherry blossom viewing spots in Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's diverse neighborhoods: visit Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) – a narrow alley packed with tiny yakitori stalls dating back to post-WWII era. Browse Isetan department store's basement food hall (depachika) for a free gourmet food tour. Walk through Kabukicho entertainment district.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the neon-lit energy of Shinjuku at night. Visit the Golden Gai area – a maze of over 200 tiny bars, each seating only 5–8 people, offering a uniquely intimate Tokyo nightlife experience. Many bars charge a small cover (¥500–¥1,000) but drinks are affordable.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku – try a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local diner (teishoku) for ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Omoide Yokocho – yakitori skewers and beer for ¥800–¥1,200 (lunch hours are quieter and sometimes cheaper)
meals.dinner: Golden Gai or nearby – small ramen shop or standing bar snacks for ¥700–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks are free and offer one of the best views in the city without paying ¥2,000+ at commercial towers. Shinjuku Gyoen closes on Mondays – check calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba – Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi (scenic ride over Rainbow Bridge, ¥330). Visit the teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum (book in advance, ¥3,200) – a world-class immersive tech-art experience perfectly aligned with tech culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (see the life-size Gundam statue outside for free), Odaiba Seaside Park (free beachfront walk with views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline), and the Venus Fort shopping mall (free entry). Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom (free) to see futuristic concept cars.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward central Tokyo. Visit Tsukiji Outer Market area for an evening stroll (the inner market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market still has shops and restaurants). Try fresh seafood at a budget restaurant near Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or konbini breakfast before heading to Odaiba
meals.lunch: Odaiba – DiverCity food court or a quick bite at a budget restaurant in the mall for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area – fresh seafood don (rice bowl) or sushi set for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be booked online in advance – they often sell out. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a scenic experience worth the fare. Odaiba has free Wi-Fi throughout the island.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by train). Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa Station (budget option: ¥1,360 one way, or buy a Tobu Nikko Pass for ¥2,720 round trip with unlimited local buses). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex – ornate and historically significant Edo-period architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the famous Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (¥300 to walk across). If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls (¥550 for the elevator to the viewpoint) – one of Japan's most beautiful waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Rest at the hotel and enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel neighborhood, trying a local family restaurant (famiresu) like Gusto or Denny's Japan for affordable set meals.

meals.breakfast: Early konbini breakfast before catching the train
meals.lunch: Nikko – bento box from a local shop near the shrine area for ¥600–¥900, or yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local Nikko specialty
meals.dinner: Near hotel – family restaurant set meal (pasta, salad, drink) for ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Start early to maximize time in Nikko – first train from Asakusa leaves around 6:30 AM. April weather in Nikko can be cooler than Tokyo, so bring a light jacket. The Tobu Nikko Pass is the best budget option for this day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka – one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful in cherry blossom season), browse Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional snacks and crafts, and admire the old wooden machiya townhouses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nezu Shrine (free entry) – a lesser-known but stunning shrine famous for its tunnel of torii gates (similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded). Walk to nearby Nezu and Sendagi neighborhoods for a quiet, authentic Tokyo experience. Visit the Shitamachi Museum in Ueno (¥300) for insight into old Tokyo life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji – a vibrant neighborhood known for its alternative culture, vintage clothing stores, and live music scene. Browse the many secondhand shops and enjoy the indie atmosphere. Find a local izakaya for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza – fresh melon bread or croquette from a local bakery for ¥150–¥300
meals.lunch: Yanaka area – menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) or soba noodles at a local restaurant for ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Koenji izakaya – set dinner with drinks for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the most authentic and budget-friendly neighborhoods in Tokyo – most attractions are free. Nezu Shrine is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid crowds. Koenji is accessible via JR Chuo Line from Shinjuku (¥160).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation in Odaiba (¥630 entry). This world-class science and technology museum features robots (including ASIMO), space exhibits, and interactive digital displays – ideal for tech culture enthusiasts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for a deeper dive into tech culture. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center and surrounding electronics markets for DIY components, vintage tech, and gadgets. Tour the floors of Yodobashi Camera mega-store. If interested, visit a maid cafe for the quintessential Akihabara experience (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink set).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kanda and Jimbocho – Tokyo's famous book district with hundreds of secondhand bookshops. Browse for manga, art books, and vintage Japanese magazines. Enjoy dinner in the Kanda area at an affordable soba or tempura restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or konbini before heading to Odaiba
meals.lunch: Miraikan museum café or a convenience store lunch to save budget (¥400–¥700)
meals.dinner: Kanda – traditional soba restaurant, kake soba or tempura soba for ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. Book tickets online to save time. Jimbocho bookshops are mostly open until 18:00–19:00. The area around Jimbocho also has great old-school coffee shops (kissaten) perfect for a reading break.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (approximately 1 hour from Tokyo via JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station, ¥940 one way). Visit the iconic Kotoku-in Temple and the Great Buddha (Daibutsu) – a 13-meter bronze statue dating to 1252 (entry ¥300). Walk through Hase-dera Temple with beautiful coastal garden views (¥400).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's Komachi-dori shopping street for local sweets and souvenirs. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine (free entry) – Kamakura's most important shrine. If time allows, hike part of the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Enjoy a relaxed evening near the hotel with dinner at a neighborhood restaurant or izakaya. Use the evening to rest and plan remaining days.

meals.breakfast: Early konbini breakfast before catching the train
meals.lunch: Kamakura – shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a local specialty, at a restaurant near Hase for ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Near hotel – local ramen shop or gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya for ¥400–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a JR Tokyo Wide Pass (¥15,000 for 3 days) if planning multiple day trips – covers Kamakura, Nikko (via JR), and more. Kamakura is very popular on weekends; visit on a weekday if possible. April weather is mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) – a beautiful traditional Japanese garden in central Tokyo with a tidal pond, tea house, and seasonal flowers. Located near Tsukiji, it offers a peaceful green escape in the middle of the city. Enjoy matcha tea at the garden's traditional tea house (¥510 including entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ginza – Tokyo's upscale shopping and arts district. Window shop along Chuo-dori, visit the free galleries in the Itoya stationery store (9 floors of beautiful Japanese stationery and crafts), and browse the free art galleries scattered throughout the neighborhood. Visit the Sony Park or Ginza Six atrium for free cultural displays.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome and Shimbashi for a local salary-man (office worker) dinner experience. The area around Shimbashi Station has dozens of small izakayas packed with Tokyo workers after hours – authentic, lively, and very affordable.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market – fresh tamagoyaki (egg roll), tuna onigiri, and green tea for ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Ginza – basement food hall of a department store for affordable gourmet bento boxes (¥500–¥900)
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya – yakitori, fried chicken, edamame, and draft beer for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens can be reached by water bus from Asakusa (¥800–¥1,200) for a scenic Tokyo Bay cruise – a great budget splurge. Ginza galleries are free and often feature high-quality contemporary Japanese art.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not visited earlier) or explore the Toyosu Market (the new Tsukiji) – book a tuna auction viewing in advance (free but limited spots, register online months ahead). Alternatively, visit the Toyosu Market outer area for fresh seafood at affordable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nakameguro – a trendy, photogenic neighborhood along the Meguro River, lined with cherry trees (beautiful in April even after peak bloom). Browse the boutique shops, independent cafes, and vintage stores along the canal. Visit the Nakameguro Tsutaya Books for a browse through beautifully curated Japanese design and art books.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daikanyama – adjacent to Nakameguro and one of Tokyo's most stylish neighborhoods. Explore the Log Road shopping area and enjoy a final special dinner at a mid-range restaurant to celebrate your penultimate night in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or konbini breakfast
meals.lunch: Nakameguro – a local café lunch set (sandwich, salad, coffee) for ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Daikanyama – slightly splurge on a nice Japanese set dinner (teishoku) at a local restaurant for ¥1,200–¥1,800 as a farewell treat

day_by_day.notes: Nakameguro is accessible via the Tokyu Toyoko Line from Shibuya (¥130). The canal walk is especially magical in the evening with café lights reflecting on the water. April may still have some late cherry blossoms along the river.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo – revisit a favorite neighborhood or check off any remaining items on your list. Visit Kappabashi Kitchenware Street (near Asakusa) – Tokyo's wholesale kitchen supply district where you can buy authentic Japanese knives, ceramics, chopsticks, and the famous plastic food display models as unique souvenirs at wholesale prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to the hotel, check out, and collect luggage. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Don Quijote (Donki) – a discount variety store open 24 hours with everything from snacks to electronics at low prices. Great for picking up Japanese candy, cosmetics, and unique gifts. Make your way to the airport with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Use remaining Suica card balance on train fare to the airport or refund it at a station service counter (minus ¥220 handling fee). Enjoy a final airport meal at one of the terminal restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Last konbini breakfast or a sit-down tamago gohan (egg on rice) at a local diner for ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Kappabashi area – a quick bowl of udon or soba for ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Airport terminal – treat yourself to a proper ramen or sushi set at the airport restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500 as a final Japanese meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transit, check-in, and security. Claim consumption tax refunds (8–10%) at the airport tax refund counter if you made tax-free purchases. Suica cards can be refunded or kept for future trips to Japan.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Haneda or Narita Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the hotel amenities.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport's convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) — try an onigiri rice ball, instant ramen, or a bento box for an authentic first taste of Japan

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout Tokyo. Download Google Maps offline and the Japan Official Travel App. Exchange some yen at the airport for small cash purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a relaxed start, head to the hotel breakfast and then take a gentle walk around the local neighborhood to get your bearings. Explore nearby convenience stores and any local parks or riverside paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Odaiba, a futuristic island district easily accessible from central Tokyo. Stroll along the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and the iconic life-size Gundam statue — a perfect first taste of Tokyo's tech and pop culture scene.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Odaiba at Aqua City or Venus Fort mall's dining floors, then return to the hotel for an early night to beat jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Japanese morning set (tamago sando, miso soup, coffee)
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Odaiba restaurant — budget around ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) at Maisen or a similar mid-range restaurant in Odaiba — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — check if sakura are still blooming and plan a quick detour to a nearby park. Keep the day relaxed to fully adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 7:00–8:00 AM to catch the market at its liveliest. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled egg omelette), grilled seafood skewers, and fresh oysters from the stalls. This is Tokyo's most iconic culinary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, walk or take a short taxi to Ginza — Tokyo's upscale shopping and culture district. Window shop along Chuo-dori, visit the free observation deck at the Itoya stationery flagship, and explore the Sony Park or Uniqlo flagship store for mid-range shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi for dinner, then enjoy the illuminated Hamarikyu Gardens (open until 17:00) or a cocktail at a rooftop bar with skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls — fresh sushi breakfast set and tamagoyaki (¥1,500–¥2,500 total for tastings)
meals.lunch: Soba noodles at a traditional soba-ya in Ginza — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers at an izakaya in Shimbashi — a salaryman's paradise with grilled chicken, vegetables, and cold beer (¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open daily and most stalls operate from 5:00 AM to around noon. Go early for the best selection. Bring cash as many stalls are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk — arrive at dawn (around 6:00–7:00 AM) before the crowds descend. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Gate, along Nakamise-dori shopping street, and into the main temple hall. The early morning light and incense smoke create an unforgettable atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa neighborhood on foot. Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in nearby Ryogoku to understand Tokyo's historical transformation, or browse the traditional craft shops along Kappabashi (Kitchen Town) for unique culinary souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Asakusa subway line to Akihabara for an evening stroll through the neon-lit electronics district. Browse multi-story arcades, anime shops, and maid cafés for a first taste before tomorrow's deep dive.

meals.breakfast: Ningyo-yaki (traditional doll-shaped cakes) and matcha from a Nakamise-dori stall — light and authentic (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Tempura teishoku (set meal) at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa — a legendary local institution (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Curry rice at a cozy Akihabara curry shop or a ramen bar — budget ¥900–¥1,400

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, but the grounds are most magical at dawn. Wear comfortable shoes as Asakusa involves significant walking on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Deep Dive — spend the morning immersed in Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Explore Yodobashi Akiba (the massive multi-story electronics megastore), browse retro game shops, and visit Akihabara's Radio Kaikan for anime figures and collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara — visit a maid café for a uniquely Japanese pop-culture experience, then head to the Akihabara UDX building's tech showcases. Walk south to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda for contemporary digital art exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Kanda/Jimbocho neighborhood for a relaxed evening among Tokyo's famous secondhand bookshops, then dinner in the area before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — grab an egg salad sandwich and canned coffee for the full Tokyo salaryman experience
meals.lunch: Akihabara electric town food floor — try a Japanese-style hamburger steak (hambagu) set meal (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Sukiyaki or shabu-shabu at a mid-range hot pot restaurant in Kanda — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Maid café experiences typically cost ¥1,000–¥2,000 for a drink and a performance. @Home Café and Maidreamin are popular beginner-friendly options. Most Akihabara shops open around 10:00–11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — book tickets online well in advance as they sell out weeks ahead. Arrive at opening time for the most immersive experience. Wander through the interconnected rooms of flowing digital waterfalls, luminous forests, and interactive light installations where art and technology blur.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the surrounding Toyosu or Ariake waterfront area. Visit the Toyosu Market observation deck (free) to see the world's largest fish market from above, or relax at the Toyosu LaLaport shopping complex.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Yurikamome monorail back through Odaiba for stunning sunset views over Tokyo Bay. Dinner in Odaiba with views of Rainbow Bridge lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a Toyosu area café before TeamLab opens
meals.lunch: Sushi at Toyosu Market's sushi restaurants — fresh and excellent quality (¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki (savory Japanese pancake) at a teppanyaki restaurant in Odaiba — interactive and delicious (¥1,800–¥2,800)

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online in advance at borderless.teamlab.art. Cost is approximately ¥3,200 per adult. The experience typically takes 2–3 hours. No bags larger than A4 size are permitted inside.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Harajuku and Meiji Shrine — begin with a serene walk through the forested path leading to Meiji Jingu Shrine, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Participate in a purification ritual and observe traditional ceremonies if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Meiji Shrine through Yoyogi Park (perfect for cherry blossom viewing in April) to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for colorful youth fashion, crepes, and quirky shops. Then explore the more upscale Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — for design stores and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing experience at night. View it from the Shibuya Sky observation deck or the free Mag's Park rooftop at Shibuya 109. Explore the vibrant nightlife streets around Shibuya.

meals.breakfast: Fruit crêpe from a Harajuku street stall — the original Harajuku crêpe experience (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Udon at a standing udon bar near Harajuku station — hearty and affordable (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) at Uobei or Genki Sushi in Shibuya — fun, fast, and budget-friendly (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter and open from sunrise to sunset. Yoyogi Park is a great spot for a picnic if the weather is fine. Shibuya Sky observation deck costs ¥2,000 and requires advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with a visit to the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for panoramic city views (opens at 9:00 AM). Then walk through the serene Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks and a top cherry blossom spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the Shinjuku tech and electronics scene at Yodobashi Camera Multimedia Akiba or BIC Camera. Explore the unique multi-story Tokyu Hands lifestyle store for Japanese gadgets and innovative products. Browse the narrow alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Kabukicho, Tokyo's entertainment district, and the neon-soaked Robot Restaurant area (book in advance for the Robot Restaurant show if interested). Alternatively, enjoy a quieter evening in the Golden Gai area — a labyrinth of tiny, intimate bars.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) morning set near Shinjuku station — toast, egg, and coffee (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya — an iconic, affordable Tokyo lunch (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — grilled skewers and cold beer in a smoky, atmospheric alley (¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen admission is ¥500. The Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free but may be closed on some Mondays. Golden Gai bars are tiny and intimate — most welcome tourists but have a cover charge of ¥500–¥1,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Stroll through the historic cemetery, browse Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, and soak in the atmosphere of old Edo-era Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno Park and museum district. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000 admission) for an outstanding collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, and cultural artifacts. The park itself is beautiful in April with late-blooming sakura.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) market street near Ueno station for street food and bargain shopping, then head back toward the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi-katsu (fried minced meat cutlet) from a local butcher stall (¥200–¥400)
meals.lunch: Bento box from a Yanaka specialty shop or a teishoku set meal at a local restaurant (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ in Ueno's Koreatown (Shin-Okubo is nearby) — tabletop grilling with galbi and samgyeopsal (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Ueno Park is a short walk from Yanaka and makes a pleasant afternoon stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (approximately 2 hours). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex, one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrines, surrounded by ancient cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate, and the tranquil Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel to rest after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — Nikko's local specialty — at a restaurant near the shrine complex (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Simple Japanese set meal near the hotel — grilled fish teishoku or udon (¥1,000–¥1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (approximately ¥4,780) for unlimited travel on Tobu lines and buses within Nikko. Tosho-gu admission is ¥1,300. Start early (depart by 7:00–8:00 AM) to maximize time in Nikko.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood beloved for vintage clothing shops, independent cafés, live music venues, and a creative, artsy atmosphere. Browse the dozens of vintage and thrift stores for unique fashion finds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Daikanyama and Nakameguro — two of Tokyo's trendiest neighborhoods. Visit the iconic Tsutaya Books (a beautifully designed bookstore-café), stroll along the Meguro River canal (lined with cherry trees), and browse the boutique shops and concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Nakameguro — the area has excellent mid-range restaurants. Then take an evening walk along the illuminated canal if cherry blossoms are still lingering.

meals.breakfast: Third-wave specialty coffee and avocado toast at a Shimokitazawa independent café (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.lunch: Nepalese curry or ethnic cuisine in Shimokitazawa — the neighborhood has excellent international food (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Italian-Japanese fusion or a craft burger at a Nakameguro bistro — the area has excellent mid-range dining (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa vintage shops are best browsed between 12:00–18:00 when most are open. Nakameguro canal is particularly beautiful in the evening with lantern-style lighting. Both neighborhoods are very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Roppongi — explore the Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower with its world-class contemporary art exhibitions and a free Tokyo City View observation deck. The museum often features cutting-edge digital and tech-themed art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi (free entry to building, exhibitions vary) — one of Japan's largest art facilities with stunning Kisho Kurokawa-designed architecture. Walk through the Roppongi Hills complex and browse the outdoor art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Tokyo — head to Tokyo Skytree in Asakusa for night views from 450 meters above the city (book tickets in advance, ¥3,100 for the upper deck). Celebrate with a special dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eggs Benedict or a Western-style brunch at a Roppongi café (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Ramen at a highly-rated Roppongi ramen shop — try a rich tonkotsu or spicy miso variety (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a mid-range teppanyaki restaurant near Tokyo Skytree — watch the chef cook wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on a hot iron plate (¥4,000–¥6,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets should be booked online at tokyo-skytree.jp. The view at night is extraordinary — on clear days you can see Mount Fuji. Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on most days), making it a great evening option too.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — wake up early for one last neighborhood walk. Revisit a favorite spot or explore somewhere you missed. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at a department store basement food hall (depachika) — excellent for high-quality Japanese snacks, sweets, and packaged foods to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and head to the airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse duty-free shops at the airport for final souvenir purchases — sake, Kit Kat flavors, and beauty products are popular choices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final convenience store breakfast — pick up your favorite items you discovered during the trip
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or sushi at the terminal — Narita and Haneda both have excellent food options (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange luggage storage with the hotel if your flight is in the evening. The Narita Express (N'EX) takes about 60 minutes to Narita Airport; the Tokyo Monorail or Keikyu Line takes 30–40 minutes to Haneda. Keep ¥5,000–¥10,000 cash for any final purchases or transport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have been perfecting their craft for generations and experience the authentic flavors of Tokyo's most iconic food destination.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Browse multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, explore retro game shops, visit maid cafes, and discover the latest in Japanese tech gadgets, robotics kits, and cutting-edge consumer electronics that define Japan's tech culture.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, at dawn before the crowds arrive. Stroll through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, explore the surrounding Asakusa district's old Edo-era atmosphere, and witness morning prayers and incense rituals for an authentic cultural experience.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture merge seamlessly. Walk through immersive, ever-changing rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art created by the renowned teamLab collective. A perfect fusion of Japan's tech innovation and artistic expression.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Izakaya Alley Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Venture into the narrow, lantern-lit alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and Kabukicho's hidden izakayas for an unforgettable evening of yakitori, ramen, sake, and Japanese whisky. Sit elbow-to-elbow with Tokyo locals, order seasonal small plates, and experience the convivial after-work dining culture that defines authentic Tokyo nightlife.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and decompress in your beachfront suite. Order a light late-night room service spread featuring Japanese comfort classics – ochazuke (rice with green tea), miso soup, and seasonal pickles. Enjoy a nightcap at the resort bar if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Premium room service at Aegean Bliss Resort – ochazuke, miso soup, Japanese pickles, and a curated sake or whisky nightcap

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private luxury transfer (black car or limousine service) from the airport. Request early check-in amenities such as a welcome amenity, yukata robe, and turndown service. Keep the evening light to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Ease into Tokyo with a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then take a gentle stroll along the beachfront promenade to acclimate. Visit a nearby neighborhood shotengai (traditional shopping street) for a slow, unhurried introduction to local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island, for an introductory taste of Tokyo's tech culture. Explore teamLab's Planets installation (sister venue to Borderless), the Toyota Mega Web showroom, and the iconic life-size Gundam statue. Enjoy the sweeping views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a high-end Odaiba restaurant with panoramic bay views – consider Tableaux or a kaiseki restaurant within a luxury Odaiba hotel. Return to resort early for a restful first full night.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort breakfast – Japanese and Western buffet with fresh seasonal fruit, tamagoyaki, grilled fish, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Odaiba waterfront café – light bento set or artisan sandwiches with Tokyo Bay views
meals.dinner: Upscale kaiseki or contemporary Japanese cuisine restaurant in Odaiba – multi-course omakase with seasonal ingredients and sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is easily accessible by the scenic Yurikamome monorail or a water bus from nearby piers. Jet lag may still be a factor – keep the pace relaxed. April weather is typically mild and cherry blossom season may still be active.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour – Rise early and head to Tsukiji Outer Market for an immersive guided premium food tour. Sample ultra-fresh nigiri sushi, hand-rolled tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, dashi broths, and seasonal Japanese produce. Meet artisan vendors who have operated their stalls for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, walk or taxi to Ginza – Tokyo's most prestigious luxury shopping district. Explore flagship stores of Japanese and international luxury brands, visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a Tokyo institution), and browse the Ginza Six complex with its rooftop garden and curated Japanese design boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Ginza's celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants. Options include Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (book months in advance), Sushi Saito, or Ginza Kojyu for an extraordinary omakase experience.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour – fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and market snacks as part of the tour
meals.lunch: Ginza – refined lunch at a premium soba or tempura restaurant such as Tempura Kondo or Ginza Harutaka
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred omakase dinner in Ginza – 12–20 course seasonal tasting menu with premium sake or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tsukiji food tour and Ginza dinner reservation well in advance. Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant between 6:00–9:00 AM. Dress smart-casual for Ginza dining. Many top omakase venues require reservations made 1–3 months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk – Depart at dawn (around 6:00 AM) to experience Senso-ji Temple before the crowds arrive. Walk the iconic Nakamise-dori approach in serene early morning light, participate in a temple purification ritual, and explore the surrounding Asakusa streets with their traditional crafts and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Asakusa – visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in nearby Ryogoku to understand Tokyo's rich historical evolution from Edo-period city to modern megalopolis. Alternatively, take a private rickshaw tour through Yanaka, one of Tokyo's last preserved old-town neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Shinjuku Izakaya Alley Dinner Experience – Travel to Shinjuku and venture into the lantern-lit alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane). Enjoy grilled yakitori skewers, cold Sapporo draft beer, and smoky robata-grilled vegetables in an atmospheric, intimate setting. Extend the evening with a cocktail at a sophisticated Shinjuku bar.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a Asakusa tea house – matcha, wagashi sweets, and seasonal rice porridge
meals.lunch: Asakusa or Ryogoku – premium chanko-nabe (sumo wrestler hot pot) at a traditional chanko restaurant near the Kokugikan sumo arena
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho – curated izakaya experience with yakitori, grilled offal skewers, edamame, and Japanese whisky highballs; finish with cocktails at a Shinjuku rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji at dawn is a transcendent, crowd-free experience – set an early alarm. Omoide Yokocho is intimate and cash-preferred; bring yen. April evenings in Tokyo can be cool – bring a light jacket. Shinjuku's Golden Gai area is nearby for an after-dinner bar-hopping experience.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Deep Dive – Spend the morning exploring Tokyo's legendary Electric Town. Visit multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), browse rare retro gaming arcades, explore premium anime figure shops, and visit specialist stores for robotics components and cutting-edge gadgets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara with a visit to the Maid Café district for a cultural curiosity experience, then head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda creative hub. Transition to the adjacent Kanda and Jimbocho neighborhoods for antiquarian bookshops and print culture.
day_by_day.evening: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum – Experience the world-renowned digital art installation where technology and nature merge into an immersive, boundary-free environment. Book a premium evening slot for a less crowded, more atmospheric visit with dramatic lighting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a specialty coffee and pastry at a curated Akihabara café
meals.lunch: Akihabara – premium ramen at Fuunji or a high-quality curry rice at a well-regarded Akihabara curry specialist
meals.dinner: Post-TeamLab dinner at a sophisticated Odaiba or Azabudai Hills restaurant – contemporary Japanese-French fusion with waterfront ambiance

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online in advance – premium time slots sell out quickly. Wear comfortable, slip-on shoes as some TeamLab installations require removing footwear. Akihabara is most vibrant from mid-morning onward on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku & Omotesando – Begin at the iconic Meiji Jingu Shrine for a peaceful morning forest walk and Shinto ritual observation. Then stroll down Omotesando, Tokyo's tree-lined luxury boulevard, browsing flagship architecture by Tadao Ando (Omotesando Hills) and Kengo Kuma.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku's Takeshita Street for youth pop culture, then transition to the quieter Cat Street for independent boutiques and concept stores. Visit the Ukiyo-e Ota Memorial Museum of Art for an exquisite collection of traditional Japanese woodblock prints.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omotesando or Minami-Aoyama at a premium restaurant. Consider L'Effervescence (French-Japanese haute cuisine), Narisawa (innovative Japanese cuisine), or Florilège for a Michelin-starred contemporary dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Omotesando – artisan breakfast at Bread, Espresso & or a premium hotel café with freshly baked Japanese milk bread and specialty pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Harajuku – premium crepes at Marion Crepes (iconic Harajuku experience) followed by a light lunch at a Cat Street bistro
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred contemporary Japanese or French-Japanese restaurant in Minami-Aoyama – seasonal tasting menu with natural wine or sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is serene in the morning – arrive by 8:00 AM for the quietest experience. The Omotesando area is excellent for luxury shopping if desired. April cherry blossoms may still be visible in the Meiji Jingu gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko – Depart early by private car or Shinkansen to Nikko, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Tochigi Prefecture. Explore the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, the serene Rinno-ji Temple, and the surrounding cedar forest. Nikko represents the pinnacle of Edo-period decorative architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko – walk across the sacred Shinkyo Bridge, visit the Futarasan-jinja Shrine, and take a scenic stroll along the Daiya River. If time permits, visit the Nikko Tamozawa Imperial Villa for an insight into imperial Japanese life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet, indulgent dinner at the resort or a nearby premium restaurant. Consider a relaxing onsen (hot spring) bath at the resort or a nearby luxury onsen facility to soothe the day's walking.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast or a bento box prepared for the journey
meals.lunch: Nikko – traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a historic Nikko restaurant such as Gyoshintei, a specialty of the region
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby luxury dining venue – light Japanese dinner with seasonal sashimi, grilled wagyu, and vegetable tempura

day_by_day.notes: Book a private car or hire a knowledgeable guide for Nikko to maximize the experience. The journey from Tokyo is approximately 2 hours by limited express train. Nikko can be crowded on weekends – a Tuesday visit is ideal. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya & Daikanyama – Start at Shibuya Crossing, the world's busiest pedestrian scramble, for an iconic Tokyo moment. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for 360-degree panoramic views of the city. Explore the newly developed Shibuya Stream and Scramble Square complexes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent Daikanyama neighborhood – Tokyo's most refined and understated luxury enclave. Browse the Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) complex, a beautifully designed bookstore-café hybrid surrounded by architecture and culture. Explore independent fashion boutiques and design studios.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Ebisu or Daikanyama area at a premium restaurant. Consider Chateau Restaurant Joël Robuchon at Ebisu Garden Place, a spectacular French fine dining experience housed in a mock-French château, or a premium yakiniku (grilled wagyu) experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a specialty coffee and egg sandwich at a Shibuya third-wave coffee shop
meals.lunch: Daikanyama – light lunch at a Daikanyama T-Site café or a premium sandwich and natural wine bar in the neighborhood
meals.dinner: Ebisu – Joël Robuchon Tokyo or a premium A5 wagyu yakiniku restaurant with tableside grilling and sommelier-curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic at dusk when neon lights illuminate the intersection. Daikanyama is best explored on foot at a leisurely pace. Book Joël Robuchon well in advance – it is one of Tokyo's most prestigious dining addresses.

day_by_day.morning: Roppongi Art Triangle – Begin at the Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills, featuring contemporary Japanese and international art with extraordinary city views. Visit the adjacent Mori Digital Art Museum for a tech-meets-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi's art triangle – Japan's largest exhibition space with rotating world-class exhibitions. Then explore the Azabudai Hills development, Tokyo's newest luxury mixed-use complex featuring curated galleries, international restaurants, and innovative architecture by Heatherwick Studio.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Roppongi's sophisticated nightlife – begin with cocktails at a rooftop bar such as The Tokyo EDITION Toranomon Sky Bar or the Park Hyatt New York Bar (made famous by Lost in Translation). Enjoy a late dinner at a premium Roppongi restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a quiet café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills – premium lunch at one of the complex's curated restaurants, such as a French brasserie or Japanese contemporary dining
meals.dinner: Azabudai Hills or Roppongi – premium dinner at a celebrated restaurant followed by cocktails at the Park Hyatt New York Bar

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum offers a combined ticket with Tokyo City View observation deck – highly recommended at sunset. Roppongi's art triangle (Mori, National Art Center, Suntory Museum) is best covered over a full day. The Park Hyatt New York Bar requires smart dress.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka & Nezu – Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's last preserved shitamachi (old downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander the historic cemetery, browse independent craft shops along Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and visit local temples and shrines at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Shrine – a stunning vermilion torii gate tunnel shrine predating Kyoto's famous Fushimi Inari, far less crowded and equally beautiful. Continue to Ueno Park and the Tokyo National Museum – Japan's oldest and largest museum housing an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, and Buddhist sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private in-suite kaiseki dinner arranged through the resort, or visit a nearby premium sushi counter for an intimate omakase experience.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka – traditional Japanese breakfast at a century-old kissaten (coffee shop) or a local neighborhood café
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza – menchi katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet) from a local butcher, seasonal onigiri, and artisan sweets from neighborhood vendors
meals.dinner: Private in-suite kaiseki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort or an intimate 8-seat omakase sushi counter nearby

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored without a strict schedule – allow yourself to wander. The Tokyo National Museum's Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is the must-see building. Book the in-suite kaiseki dinner with the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hakone – Depart by Romancecar (luxury express train) from Shinjuku to Hakone. On clear days, enjoy spectacular views of Mount Fuji. Visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum, an extraordinary sculpture park combining modern art with mountain landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hakone – take the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani valley with sulfurous steam vents, then cruise Lake Ashi on a replica pirate ship with views of Fuji. Visit the Hakone Shrine torii gate rising from the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury ryokan (traditional inn) in Hakone for an overnight stay – Gora Kadan or Hakone Suishoen are exceptional choices. Enjoy a private kaiseki dinner in your room, followed by a private rotenburo (outdoor hot spring bath) under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure or a premium bento on the Romancecar
meals.lunch: Hakone – light lunch at the Hakone Open-Air Museum café or a mountain restaurant with Fuji views
meals.dinner: Multi-course kaiseki dinner at the ryokan – 12-course seasonal menu featuring local Hakone ingredients, mountain vegetables, and fresh river fish, served in your private tatami room

day_by_day.notes: Book the luxury ryokan well in advance – Gora Kadan and Hakone Suishoen are among Japan's finest. The Romancecar from Shinjuku offers reserved seating and panoramic windows. Mount Fuji visibility is weather-dependent – April offers reasonable odds. Pack a small overnight bag.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at dawn in Hakone for a private sunrise rotenburo (outdoor onsen bath) with potential Fuji views. Enjoy a traditional Japanese ryokan breakfast served in your room – grilled fish, miso soup, pickles, rice, and seasonal accompaniments. Explore the ryokan's gardens before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by Romancecar. Upon arrival, visit the newly opened Azabudai Hills complex or spend the afternoon at the Prada Aoyama building and surrounding high-design architecture in Minami-Aoyama. Visit the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Roppongi for cutting-edge Japanese design exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants. Consider Quintessence (French haute cuisine, 3 Michelin stars), Den (innovative Japanese, perennially ranked in Asia's 50 Best), or a private omakase counter of your choice.

meals.breakfast: Traditional ryokan breakfast in your tatami room – grilled fish, dashimaki tamago, miso soup, pickles, rice, and green tea
meals.lunch: Return journey snack or a light lunch in Minami-Aoyama at a premium café
meals.dinner: Celebratory Michelin-starred dinner at Quintessence, Den, or a top-tier omakase venue – reserve months in advance

day_by_day.notes: The ryokan morning experience (dawn onsen + traditional breakfast) is one of Japan's most memorable travel moments – do not rush it. Confirm Tokyo dinner reservations weeks or months in advance. The Romancecar return journey offers scenic valley views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo – enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast and take a last beachfront walk. Visit a nearby neighborhood market or artisan shop for final souvenir purchases. Consider a morning tea ceremony experience at a traditional tea house if not yet experienced during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time – visit any remaining wish-list spots such as the teamLab Planets in Toyosu, the Nezu Museum's exquisite Japanese garden, or a final luxury department store visit to Isetan Shinjuku for curated Japanese food gifts and premium souvenirs from the basement food hall (depachika).
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation – arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport's premium dining level (Narita and Haneda both have excellent restaurant options) before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – savor a full Japanese breakfast with seasonal items, freshly brewed coffee, and a farewell toast
meals.lunch: Isetan Shinjuku depachika (basement food hall) – curated bento, premium wagashi sweets, and artisan Japanese snacks
meals.dinner: Airport premium dining – high-quality sushi or ramen at Narita/Haneda airport's top-tier restaurant level, or an early dinner near the hotel before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and immigration. Isetan Shinjuku's basement food hall is one of the world's finest for premium Japanese food gifts. Pre-arrange luggage forwarding (takkyubin service) to the airport the day before for seamless travel. Request a late checkout from the resort if possible.
